definitions.explanation: In baseball, the count when the batter has taken three pitches called as balls. From this count, one more ball results in a walk (フォアボール), so a スリーボール count puts the pitcher under pressure. Often used as part of the full count phrase スリーボール・ツーストライク (a 3-2 "full" count).

examples.japanese: カウントはスリーボール。
スリーボールから{投|な}げるのは{難|むずか}しい。
examples.english: It's hard to pitch from a three-ball count.

examples.japanese: スリーボール・ツーストライクのフルカウントになった。
examples.english: It became a full count of three balls and two strikes.

examples.japanese: スリーボールに{追|お}い{込|こ}まれたピッチャーは{慎重|しんちょう}にコースをついて{投|な}げた。
examples.english: Driven into a three-ball count, the pitcher carefully aimed his pitches at the corners of the strike zone.

notes:
スリーボール is a wasei-eigo (Japanese-made English) baseball term meaning a count of three balls. It is heard mainly in TV/radio commentary, in baseball video games, and in casual baseball talk. In English-language baseball, the count is simply expressed as "three balls" or as part of a count like "3-2."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- カウントはスリーボール: the count is three balls
- スリーボールから{投|な}げる: to pitch from a 3-ball count
- スリーボール・ノーストライク: 3-0 count
- スリーボール・ツーストライク: 3-2 count (the same as フルカウント, "full count")
- スリーボールに{追|お}い{込|こ}まれる: to be cornered into a 3-ball count

RELATED WORDS:
- ツーストライク: two strikes
- フルカウント: full count (3 balls and 2 strikes)
- フォアボール: walk / base on balls
- ボールカウント: ball-strike count
- ストライク: strike
- ボール: ball (a pitch outside the strike zone)

USAGE:
- In Japanese broadcasts the count is conventionally given balls-first: スリーボール・ツーストライク (3-2). MLB-style English counts give strikes-first ("3 and 2" still works because it is balls-first too, but "two strikes, three balls" would sound odd).
- スリーボール is also very common in baseball manga and anime as a way of building tension before the next pitch.
